comments.content: StrictMode double-invokes effects in development only. For production, gate your fetch with a ref or AbortController, or move to a data-fetching library that handles dedupe.
The double call is intentional to surface impure effects. Keep the cleanup symmetric (cancel the request) and the duplicate call is harmless in dev.
I switch off StrictMode in production builds; it never runs there anyway. The real fix is making your effect idempotent.
Use Collectors.groupingBy with a LinkedHashMap supplier to preserve insertion order, then map each value to its size.
groupingBy with counting() as downstream collector keeps it declarative and stream-safe.
@Transactional is proxied and self-invocation bypasses it. Move the async call into a separate bean, or use TransactionTemplate inside the async method.
Also note: async methods run in a different thread, so the transaction boundary from the caller does not propagate. Handle rollback inside the async task.
Adding @Async to a public method on a separate @Service and calling it via the injected proxy fixes both problems at once.
auto-fit collapses empty tracks; auto-fill keeps them. With minmax(250px, 1fr), auto-fit usually looks better for card galleries.
auto-fill preserves the column count when there are few items, so empty tracks remain. Great when you want a fixed grid feel.
httpOnly + Secure + SameSite cookies for the refresh token, with rotation and reuse detection. Keep the access token short-lived.
Store refresh tokens server-side keyed by a hashed token; revoke on rotation. This stops replay if a token leaks.
Turn on Hibernate format_sql and trace logging, then watch the query count. fetch join solves most to-one paths; batch fetching handles collections.
@EntityGraph covers the full graph in one query. Just avoid pagination on the collection side or you get in-memory pagination.
Split the context by domain slice and memoize providers. Consumers only subscribe to the slice they read, so unrelated updates do not re-render them.
Context value identity matters: memoize the object with useMemo or every consumer re-renders on each provider render.
eclipse-temurin + jlink custom runtime dropped my image from 500MB to ~120MB. Then strip debug symbols and use layer caching.
Copy the built jar in its own RUN layer so Gradle/Maven changes do not invalidate the app layer. Smallest is not always fastest to start.
